Guests lingered talking after the Prophet's wedding feast for Zainab, his most lavish, until he hung a curtain and the verse on entering his houses only when invited came down.
On journeys let camels graze in fertile land, hurry through barren land and do not camp on the road at night; travel is a hardship, so hurry home when done.
Cover vessels, tie waterskins, shut doors naming Allah, and put out lamps and fires at night; keep children in at nightfall when Satan roams; a yearly pestilence enters uncovered vessels.

The Prophet commanded visiting the sick, following funerals, answering sneezers, fulfilling vows, helping the poor, accepting invitations and greeting, and forbade gold rings, silver vessels, silk saddle cloths and silk.
The Prophet forbade eating left-handed, walking in one sandal, wrapping oneself with no opening for the arms, and sitting with a single garment wrapped round the knees, which may expose.
Lying on one's back with one foot over the other was forbidden, yet the Prophet was seen lying that way in the mosque.
Those who must sit on the paths should give the path its rights: lowering the gaze, causing no harm, exchanging greetings, and commanding good and forbidding evil.
The Prophet told people to avoid sitting on the paths or else give them their rights: lowering the gaze, causing no harm, returning greetings, good talk, commanding good, forbidding evil.
Of three men reaching the Prophet's circle, one took a gap and Allah sheltered him, one sat behind from shyness, and one left, so Allah turned away from him.
No one may make another rise to take his seat, even on Friday, but should say 'make room'; one who leaves his place and returns has most right to it.
In a vision, as the Prophet used a miswak, two men vied for it; he gave it to the younger but was told to give it to the elder.
